title: Between Formal and Casual
text:
Language registers shift according to audience, setting, and purpose. A formal letter to a government office uses full sentences, precise vocabulary, and a respectful distance. A message to a friend, by contrast, may contain contractions, slang, and abbreviated phrases that signal familiarity.

Skilled writers move deliberately along this spectrum. They may begin a report in a formal tone and then introduce a more conversational sentence to make a point memorable. Such shifts are effective only when they are intentional, because an unexpected change of register can confuse or alienate the reader.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what does a formal letter to a government office typically use?
What may a skilled writer do in a report, according to paragraph two?
options: Introduce a conversational sentence to make a point memorable
Remove every sentence from the report

questions.text: Why do intentional shifts in register work well, according to the passage?
options: Because they make every text informal
Because an unexpected change can confuse or alienate the reader
Because they are required by government offices

questions.text: What can be inferred about the writer's awareness of the audience?
options: It does not matter who reads the text
It is essential for choosing an appropriate register
It prevents the use of any conversational language

vocabulary.definition: varieties of language used in particular situations
shortened forms of words, such as 'don't'
done on purpose and with careful thought
cause someone to feel distant or unwelcome
